mechanism_narrative: A sustained federal funds rate below 4.0% indicates accommodative monetary policy that lowers discount rates for equity valuation, producing positive S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: SPX 20-day returns are negative in more than 55% of periods when FEDFUNDS remains below 4.0%.

mechanism_narrative: When the federal funds rate exceeds 5.0%, restrictive monetary policy increases discount rates and compresses equity valuations, causing negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: SPX 20-day returns are positive in more than 45% of periods when FEDFUNDS exceeds 5.0%.

mechanism_narrative: A combination of unemployment rate below 4.0% and federal funds rate above 5.0% signals an overheating economy with restrictive policy, triggering negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: SPX 20-day returns are positive in more than 50% of periods when UNRATE < 4.0% and FEDFUNDS > 5.0%.

mechanism_narrative: In late-cycle expansion regimes, housing starts below 1600.0 thousand units signal weakening consumer demand, causing negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 60 trading days.
failure_condition: SPX 60-day returns are positive in more than 55% of periods when HOUST < 1600.0 and the regime is late-cycle expansion.

mechanism_narrative: A sustained industrial production index above 110.0 indicates robust manufacturing output, supporting corporate earnings growth and producing positive S&P 500 forward returns over the next 5 trading days.

failure_condition: SPX 20-day returns are positive in more than 45% of periods when UNRATE < 4.0%.

failure_condition: SPX 20-day returns are positive in more than 50% of periods when HOUST < 1600.0 and RSAFS < 370000.0.
